teaser.text: Intuitive Surgical sells hospitals the equipment and supplies behind robot-assisted surgery and robotic lung biopsy. Its business begins with a system, but it earns durable revenue when trained teams use that system and reorder the tools and support that make each case possible.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Intuitive Surgical?

paragraphs.text: The bear case begins with the same revenue base but uses 8% growth, then 10%. It returns to 8% in the final year because U.S. procedure growth was about 12%, hospitals may defer elective cases, and trade-ins may replace capacity. Margins fall from 25.0% to 24.5%, so earnings run from $3,125 million to $3,638 million. The bull case uses 20% growth, then 19%, and 17%, with margins rising from 28.0% to 30.0%. Ion adoption, da Vinci 5 utilization, and manufacturing scale support that path. Earnings rise from $3,898 million to $5,814 million.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Intuitive Surgical really make?

paragraphs.text: Stock compensation adds a shareholder cost that conventional free cash flow does not deduct. Subtracting $788.2 million of stock pay leaves “real free cash flow” of $1,702.5 million. That measure asks how much cash remains after recognizing the ownership transferred to employees.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Intuitive Surgical today?

paragraphs.text: The 48.1x trailing P/E means investors pay $48.10 for each dollar of recent earnings. EBITDA removes depreciation, interest, and taxes, so it can make a business with expensive equipment look more cash-generative than it is. Replacing or expanding those robots still requires cash. Free cash flow makes that test more directly by subtracting capital spending.

blocks.heading: What has Intuitive Surgical guided for 2026?

paragraphs.text: Management’s July 16 guidance calls for worldwide da Vinci procedure growth of 13.5%–15.5% in 2026, near the midpoint. It held that range while raising expected non-GAAP gross margin to 68.0%–69.0% and narrowing expected non-GAAP operating-expense growth to 11.0%–13.0%. Non-GAAP figures adjust standard accounting results for items such as share-based compensation and unusual charges, so they describe management’s view of ongoing operations rather than the exact profit shareholders receive.

blocks.heading: Has Intuitive Surgical kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: There is evidence that management delivered on important commitments. Management first forecast da Vinci procedure growth between 15.5% and 17%. The eventual result was 18%, and da Vinci 5 moved into broad U.S. launch. Those outcomes support the execution record because they connect pay to adoption and product delivery.

blocks.heading: What were Intuitive Surgical's revenue and profit trends over the last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: Revenue reached $2,892.3 million and operating income reached $971.9 million. Instruments and accessories, systems, and service all grew, so the result was broad rather than dependent on one line.

blocks.heading: What should people watch in Intuitive Surgical's next results?

paragraphs.text: On October 20, investors should separate da Vinci from Ion, Intuitive’s platform for lung biopsies. In Q2, worldwide da Vinci procedures grew approximately 15%, while Ion grew approximately 36%. Da Vinci growth was 12% in the United States against 20% outside it. Broad growth across specialties would provide stronger evidence than a temporary surge in postponed cases.

The next step is utilization: procedures per installed system. June’s installed base reached 11,710 da Vinci systems and 1,096 Ion systems. Management reported Q2 utilization increases of 3% for da Vinci and 11% for Ion. Rising procedures and rising utilization suggest hospitals are using their investments more intensively, although neither proves that a hospital’s reimbursement covers its full cost.
